summary: NASA and Boeing are preparing to present an operational update on the Starliner crew capsule program as international cooperation under the U.S.-led lunar exploration framework expands, with San Marino and Côte d’Ivoire becoming the newest signatories to the Artemis Accords. In commercial space industry developments, satellite technology firm Hubble Network secured $200 million in Series C funding at a $1.6 billion valuation, component manufacturer Moog completed a clean room facility in Niagara Falls to scale up thruster production, and a private spacecraft fell back to Earth after failing in its attempt to rescue an aging NASA space telescope. Military aviation and defense space activities saw the U.S. Air Force certify Anduril’s Barracuda cruise missile for open system updates and allocate $87 million toward F-16 electronic warfare system upgrades, while the service completed the final flight of its legacy HH-60G Pave Hawk combat rescue helicopter. In space science, scientific analysis from the James Webb Space Telescope revealed atmospheric ammonia and unexpected cold temperatures on an exoplanet giant, while separate JWST observations confirmed that early cosmic galaxies were already seeding the universe with heavy elements. Looking ahead, readers should watch for NASA leadership to deliver a promised "Artemis Acceleration" program update next month.
